prompt: Which statement is the CONTRAPOSITIVE of "If a shape is a square, then it has four sides"?

choices.label: If a shape does not have four sides, then it is not a square
If a shape has four sides, then it is a square
If a shape is not a square, then it does not have four sides
A shape is a square if and only if it has four sides

hint: The contrapositive does two things at once, not just one.

hints.text: The contrapositive does two things at once, not just one.
Swap the two parts AND negate both: "if not $q$, then not $p$."
Not four sides ⇒ not a square. That is choice A.

explanation: For "if $p$, then $q$," the contrapositive is "if not $q$, then not $p$" — swapped and negated.
Here $p$ is "is a square" and $q$ is "has four sides," so the contrapositive is "if a shape does not have four sides, then it is not a square."
Choice B is the converse, choice C is the inverse, and choice D is a biconditional. Only the contrapositive is guaranteed to have the same truth value as the original — and this one is clearly true.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sanity-check the truth values
steps: The original is true: every square really does have four sides.
A contrapositive must also be true. Choice A is true; choice B is false (a rectangle has four sides but is not a square); choice C is false for the same rectangle. That leaves A.
